key_patterns: VERIFIED NEXT 16 NONCE CONTRACT (from node_modules/next/dist/server/app-render/app-render.js:209 + get-script-nonce-from-header.js): app-render reads the INCOMING REQUEST header 'content-security-policy' (falls back to 'content-security-policy-report-only'), finds the 'script-src' directive, and extracts the FIRST source matching /^'nonce-([A-Za-z0-9+/_-]+={0,2})'$/. It then applies nonce= to all framework/hydration/injected scripts and to Next-injected styles and <Script nonce> components. Therefore proxy.ts must (a) generate a per-request base64 nonce, (b) build a CSP string containing script-src 'self' 'nonce-<value>' (prod) or +'unsafe-eval' (dev), (c) set that CSP on request headers via NextResponse.next({ request: { headers } }) so app-render sees it, AND (d) set the same CSP + an x-nonce header on the RESPONSE for browser enforcement. Next.js official guide confirms this middleware/proxy pattern (also sets custom x-nonce header). Nonce requires DYNAMIC rendering; pages are dynamic here (JWT auth), and proxy.ts matcher already excludes _next/static & static assets. INLINE SOURCE INVENTORY: no first-party inline <script> with raw JS (only <script src='/dark-reader-cleanup.js'> which is script-src 'self'); Sentry loads as bundles. Inline STYLE via <style dangerouslySetInnerHTML> exists in server components components/branding/branding-provider.tsx and components/shared/branded-header.tsx (tenant branding), plus next/font injected styles and react-hot-toast inline style attributes. These are why style-src 'unsafe-inline' removal is fragile.
